races.title: State House, District 52
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Ben Moss
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 52, in office since 2021 (first elected in the old District 66). Railroad engineer from Rockingham and small business owner. Served on the Richmond County Board of Commissioners from 2010 to 2020. Chairs the House Wildlife Resources Committee.

endorsements.text: His campaign site says he was previously endorsed by Grass Roots NC and the National Rifle Association (NRA). These are the campaign's own claims, with no year given.
2026 endorsement listed by Ballotpedia: The Civic Table (Sway voting group by Carrie Jackson).

cands.gaps: We could not find when, or whether, Ben Moss moved anywhere, since sources describe him as a lifelong Rockingham resident. We found no documented actions, such as sponsored bills or official records, on data centers, homestead property taxes, land buying by out-of-state or foreign buyers, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, school choice or teacher pay. His positions on guns, abortion and policing come only from his own campaign site, as general statements. We found no public statements by him on data centers or development. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in any year. We found no reporting on controversies and no foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Rockingham, NC, and his campaign site says he is a lifelong Rockingham resident who graduated from Richmond Senior High School.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State House member since 2021; Richmond County commissioner 2010–2020; career railroad engineer (CSX) and small business owner.
qual.why: He has about five years of legislative service and a decade in local elected office, plus business ownership. Committee seats and chairs were not counted. No law, policy or budget career outside elected office was found, so the score sits at the low end of the high range.

cands.name: Joe Parfitt
cands.bio: Retired U.S. Army soldier (1999–2020) who served as an airborne infantryman and Civil Affairs operator. Now a public school teacher in Moore County, living in Southern Pines. Previously worked in finance and construction. Vice chair of his local precinct. Democratic nominee for NC House District 52 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Says he is endorsed by VoteVets, Planned Parenthood and the North Carolina Democratic Party (self-reported in his Ballotpedia survey).
Recommended by the Sway voting groups Fair Map Fight Club, The Civic Table, and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy.

cands.gaps: We found no stated position from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing, or gun policy. We found no documented actions in office, since he has not held office. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had. His exact birthplace and the year he finished each degree beyond what Ballotpedia lists are not stated. His Army rank and specific duties are not detailed beyond his campaign site's description.

local.label: Roots 40: His campaign site says he was born and raised in eastern Pennsylvania, was stationed at Fort Bragg in 2011, and now lives in Southern Pines, so he has been in North Carolina about 15 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served in the U.S. Army 1999–2020, worked in finance and construction after retiring, and now teaches in Moore County Schools. He is vice chair of his local precinct and has held no elected office.
qual.why: He has no legislative, policy or budget career and has held no elected office. His work history is military service, finance, construction and teaching, which is not directly related to writing law and budgets.
